purpose: Exchange bounded rank-local target metadata and require all-rank startup validation before capture resources are connected

interfaces.coordinate_target_startup: Uses the existing PP-major/TP-minor Gloo CPU group. Votes binding/serialization, receive allocation and global validation status; exchanges bounded strict JSON; requires identical final teacher/KV/layout digests.
interfaces.CaptureStartupError: Reports phase and failed vote group ranks; remote exception text is never included.
interfaces.CaptureCoordinator.create: Loads capture configuration inside the startup callback; connects Store/Catalog resources only after identity agreement. Disabled capture skips collective work.
interfaces.TpModelWorker.init_training_capture: Supplies the existing world CPU group and actual TP/PP/DP rank coordinates.

protocol.control_header: Seven int64 CPU values: version, error flag, byte length and four signed SHA-256 words.
protocol.encoding: JSON metadata, no pickle or tensor payloads
phases: validation status and final SHA-256 agreement
protocol.transport_failure: Abort startup and tear down workers/group; no retry on the failed process group.

jobs.note: Real serving uses the existing single-rank world CPU group; AR/DSpark, graph/overlap, pressure, adaptive/latency and cache lifecycle regression passes.

gloo_observation.rank_records: Synthetic typed metadata, no distributed model forward.
gloo_observation.config_failure: Missing config file is observed inside the startup callback; Store connection is not attempted.

limits: Serving TP/PP/DP gates remain closed. The current request coordinator explicitly rejects distributed capture after startup identity agreement.
Distributed Store/resource initialization, common request configuration, admission/failure agreement, per-sample descriptors, global teacher top-128/LSE and scheduler wiring remain pending.
All group members must enter the same protocol invocation order with a valid Gloo group and valid finite timeout.
A permanently blocked local callback, initial small-control-buffer allocation failure, or a failure before process-group creation still requires the serving supervisor.
The byte caps bound encoded records and padded receive tensors, not total process/model memory or JSON object allocation.
Tests use local Gloo with synthetic records. They do not establish TP/PP numerical inference, RDMA, production Catalog integration, trained-draft quality or throughput SLOs.
Runtime integration remains TP1/PP1 on one H100 with a synthetic draft, HTTP Catalog double and local TCP Store. The existing optional cross-engine HF KV diagnostic is not enabled.
